To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the recent decline of the Italian economy must be seen as the result of the inability of the Italian institutional framework to support the country’s convergence to the technological frontier.

Italy has been characterized by sub-optimal economic performance since 1861, and that the root of the problem is to be found in a weak and/or poorly enforced set of rules that regulate economic activities, in a process of State formation, and in the post WWII politcal equilibrium.

(a) the Italian economy is in a state of structural crisis that started in the 1980’s, (b) this structural crisis is the result of the inability of the Italian economy to keep up with the technological frontier, (c) the inability of the economy to keep up the frontier is in turn the result of weak and poorly enforced rules that regulate economic activities, (d) the origin of this problem is the feature of the Italian process of state formation and the post-war political equilibrium
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of institutions in shaping long run economic performance.
the relationship between institutions and economic development.
the relationship between economic and institutional performance in Italy since 1861.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Italian economy has been a failure since the very beginning of the unified state.

the Italian economic crisis is not the result of the recent political events, but of a long-term process of institutional deterioration, which started in the late 19th Century, and was reinforced in the last 60 years.
the Italian economy is a “developmental state” in the worst sense of the term.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Italy has been unable to become a modern country because of the inability of its political institutions to create a set of rules and institutions that are congruent with the technological frontier.
“the Italian economic performance is the result of a long-term process that has its roots in the way the State has been built and the way it was run after World War II”.
the Italian economy is a victim of its institutions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Italian case is a good example of how the lack of congruence between institutions and economic performance can lead to a long-term decline.
, while the country celebrated its 150th birthday, it is still far from being able to celebrate its 100th anniversary of economic development.
the Italian economy has been, and is, a victim of the inability of the State to enforce rules that promote economic growth.
